$description: Semantic colour roles (design v6.1, after the Fluent 2 alias tokens and the Microsoft Teams layout): what a colour is for, in light and dark. Neutral first, in three layers with gentle steps between them: the content is white, supporting panes (side navigation, lists) a light grey, the global frame (top bar, app rail) a slightly darker grey. Blocks are made with thin light borders and space, never shadows (shadows only for layers above the page). Never pure black: text is a dark grey. The blue signal marks only the primary action, links, the selected item and focus; status colours only report status; orange is the brand and promo labels. Pairs that must stay readable are in contrast.json and checked by the tests.

background.$description: the content: pages and screens are white (colorNeutralBackground1)

pane.$description: a supporting pane next to the content: side navigation, list pane, filters (colorNeutralBackground3)

frame.$description: the global frame around everything: top bar, app rail (colorNeutralBackground5)

surface.$description: cards, sheets, dialogs: white, set apart by a border or by space (colorNeutralBackground1)

surfaceSubtle.$description: a quiet fill inside a surface: search field, hovered row (colorNeutralBackground2)

imageSlot.$description: an image that has not loaded or does not exist

border.$description: the outline of a card, a table, a split between panes (colorNeutralStroke2)

borderStrong.$description: outline of an input, checkbox, secondary button (colorNeutralStroke1)

accent.$description: the one primary action, the selected item, focus (colorBrandBackground)

accentSubtle.$description: selected row, chip or nav item fill

brand.$description: bonbon's own colour: logo, mascot, app icon. Never a button, never text

neutralAction.$description: a strong neutral action (dark button on marketing pages)

promo.$description: discount and voucher labels: the only orange text
